segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Katherine and today we're talking about fear.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们谈论的是恐惧。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to talk about phobias, different types of fears that you have.
segments.zh: 今天我们将讨论恐惧症，你有不同类型的恐惧。

segments.en: Many people are scared of different things and that's what we're going to talk about today.
segments.zh: 许多人害怕不同的事情，这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

segments.en: Okay, so let's listen to today's dialogue and find out what the people in our dialogue are very, very afraid of.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们听听今天的对话，找出我们对话中的人非常非常害怕的事情。

segments.en: Are you excited about your trip next month?
segments.zh: 你对下个月的旅行感到兴奋吗？

segments.en: Yes and no.
segments.zh: 既是，也不是。

segments.en: I can't wait to go to Europe, but at the same time I'm terrified.
segments.zh: 我迫不及待地想去欧洲，但同时我也很害怕。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: Well, I have aerophobia.
segments.zh: 嗯，我有飞行恐惧症。

segments.en: I have a chronic fear of flying.
segments.zh: 我对飞行有一种长期的恐惧。

segments.en: Oh really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: I have an uncle who is also terrified of flying.
segments.zh: 我有一个也害怕飞行的叔叔。

segments.en: It's not that bad though.
segments.zh: 不过也没那么糟糕。

segments.en: I mean, it is pretty scary to be up in this big machine flying through the air at 700 miles per hour.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，坐在这个以每小时 700 英里在空中飞行的大机器上，挺吓人的。

segments.en: I actually have arachnophobia.
segments.zh: 其实我有蜘蛛恐惧症。

segments.en: You're scared of spiders?
segments.zh: 你怕蜘蛛？

segments.en: I actually have two more phobias, acrophobia and glossophobia.
segments.zh: 其实我还有另外两种恐惧症：恐高症和公众演讲恐惧症。

segments.en: I guess that explains why you're afraid of flying, but public speaking is not that bad.
segments.zh: 我想这可以解释为什么你害怕飞行，但公开演讲并没有那么糟糕。

segments.en: Are you kidding?
segments.zh: 你开玩笑吧？

segments.en: When I get on stage, my palms start to sweat.
segments.zh: 当我上台时，我的手掌开始出汗。

segments.en: I get really nervous and I can hardly speak.
segments.zh: 我真的很紧张，我几乎不能说话。

segments.en: Well, I must confess that I am a bit claustrophobic.
segments.zh: 好吧，我必须承认我有点幽闭恐惧症。

segments.en: I hate being in an elevator for more than five seconds.
segments.zh: 我讨厌在电梯里呆了五秒钟以上。

segments.en: We are such weirdos, right?
segments.zh: 我们真是怪人，对吧？

segments.en: All right, we're back, so let's take a look at those phobias on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，让我们来看看语言要点的那些恐惧症。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: The first phobia that we have is called aerophobia.
segments.zh: 我们拥有的第一个恐惧症被称为 Aerophobia。

segments.en: That's right, aerophobia.
segments.zh: 没错，飞行恐惧症。

segments.en: That means that you are scared of flying.
segments.zh: 这意味着你害怕飞行。

segments.en: We can tell because phobia means fear of something, but it's not just a fear.
segments.zh: 我们可以分辨，因为恐惧症意味着对某事的恐惧，但这不仅仅是恐惧。

segments.en: It means that if you go on an airplane, you get very, very upset.
segments.zh: 这意味着如果你乘坐飞机，你会非常非常沮丧。

segments.en: You think that you're going to die.
segments.zh: 你以为你会死。

segments.en: Phobia is a very serious fear, but aero, like aeroplane, is the prefix.
segments.zh: 恐惧症是一种非常严重的恐惧，而 aero 就像 aeroplane 里的 aero 一样，是个前缀。

segments.en: Phobia is a fear of going on airplanes.
segments.zh: 恐惧症是对上飞机的恐惧。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Another phobia that we have is arachnophobia.
segments.zh: 我们的另一个恐惧症是蜘蛛恐惧症。

segments.en: Again, as you see in the prefix, arachno is related to a spider.
segments.zh: 同样，正如您在前缀中看到的，Arachno 与蜘蛛有关。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: This comes from the origins of English.
segments.zh: 这来自英语的起源。

segments.en: I'm not sure if it's Greek or Latin, but arachnophobia, like arachnid, has to do with spiders.
segments.zh: 我不确定它是希腊语还是拉丁语，但蜘蛛恐惧症，就像蜘蛛一样，与蜘蛛有关。

segments.en: I'm afraid of spiders if I have arachnophobia.
segments.zh: 如果我有蜘蛛恐惧症，我害怕蜘蛛。

segments.en: That is right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Now taking a look at two more types of phobias here, we have acrophobia and glossophobia.
segments.zh: 现在再看看这里的另外两种恐惧症，我们有恐高症和演讲恐惧症。

segments.en: Let's take a look at the first one, acrophobia.
segments.zh: 让我们来看看第一个，恐高症。

segments.en: Acrophobia has to do with heights.
segments.zh: 恐高症与高度有关。

segments.en: I don't like to be on tall buildings.
segments.zh: 我不喜欢在高楼上。

segments.en: I don't like to maybe look down from heights.
segments.zh: 我不喜欢从高处往下看。

segments.en: That means I'm afraid of heights.
segments.zh: 这意味着我恐高。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: You're afraid of being at a very high altitude, acrophobia.
segments.zh: 你害怕处于非常高的高度，恐高症。

segments.en: Now glossophobia is an interesting one because this one, you are scared of public speaking or you get very nervous when you're in front of a group of people.
segments.zh: 现在，glossophobia 是个很有意思的例子，因为这种人害怕公开演讲，或者在一群人面前时会变得非常紧张。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So this is actually a very, very common fear, but if it's a serious fear, it's a phobia.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上是一种非常非常常见的恐惧，但如果是严重的恐惧，那就是恐惧症。

segments.en: So glossophobia means that when you go in front of people, you get very, very anxious, upset, your stomach hurts, you have wet hands.
segments.zh: 所以 glossophobia 意味着，当你站到人群面前时，你会变得非常、非常焦虑、不安，胃疼，手心出汗。

segments.en: So that's a very serious fear.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常严重的恐惧。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And for our last phobia, we have claustrophobia.
segments.zh: 对于我们最后的恐惧症，我们有幽闭恐惧症。

segments.en: I think it's one of the most common ones.
segments.zh: 我认为这是最常见的一种。

segments.en: If you have claustrophobia, you're afraid of smaller tight spaces.
segments.zh: 如果你有幽闭恐惧症，你会害怕较小的狭窄空间。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So people who, so you heard the word claustrophobic, people who are claustrophobic or people who suffer from claustrophobia don't like to be in small tight places like elevators, for example, tunnels.
segments.zh: 所以，你听到了 claustrophobic 这个词——有幽闭恐惧症的人，或患有幽闭恐惧症的人，不喜欢待在电梯这样的狭小空间里，比如隧道。

segments.en: So now you brought up an interesting point.
segments.zh: 所以现在你提出了一个有趣的观点。

segments.en: Our last phobia, we said claustrophobic and now we must make the difference between, for example, claustrophobia and being claustrophobic.
segments.zh: 最后一种恐惧症，我们说了 claustrophobic，现在我们得区分一下，比如 claustrophobia 和 claustrophobic 的区别。

segments.en: So a phobia, you hear the word, you hear the ending IA, phobia, claustrophobia is a noun.
segments.zh: 所以一个恐惧症，你听到这个词，你听到的结尾是 ia，恐惧症，幽闭恐惧症是一个名词。

segments.en: That means I can talk about, I have it, I have this fear.
segments.zh: 这意味着我可以谈论，我拥有它，我有这种恐惧。

segments.en: But when you're talking about the adjective, something that describes you, you would have to use the ic ending.
segments.zh: 但是当你谈论形容词时，描述你的东西，你必须使用 IC 结尾。

segments.en: I'm claustrophobic.
segments.zh: 我有幽闭恐惧症。

segments.en: He is acrophobic.
segments.zh: 他有恐高症。

segments.en: They are aerophobic.
segments.zh: 他们有飞行恐惧症。

segments.en: Okay, so that is the adjective form.
segments.zh: 好的，这就是形容词形式。

segments.en: So if I say I have arachnophobia, it means I have this fear or I can say I am arachnophobic.
segments.zh: 所以如果我说我有蜘蛛恐惧症，就意味着我有这种恐惧，或者我可以说我害怕蜘蛛。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: So this can be used for all other kinds of phobias.
segments.zh: 所以这可以用于所有其他类型的恐惧症。

segments.en: So when you learn those words, remember that there's two different kinds.
segments.zh: 所以当你学习这些单词时，请记住有两种不同的类型。

segments.en: There's the IA, there's the IA, a phobia, which is the noun and ic, which is the adjective.
segments.zh: -ia 结尾的是名词，比如 phobia；-ic 结尾的是形容词。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So in the beginning of today's dialogue, the character said, I cannot wait to go to Europe, but at the same time, I'm terrified.
segments.zh: 所以在今天的对话开始时，角色说，我迫不及待地想去欧洲，但同时我也很害怕。

segments.en: So at the same time.
segments.zh: 所以同时。

segments.en: So in this case, we're saying that we are happy, but also we are scared.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们说我们很高兴，但我们也很害怕。

segments.en: So two things at once at the same time.
segments.zh: 所以同时发生两件事。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So this is a little bit different from when we talk about, I can do two things at the same time.
segments.zh: 所以这与我们谈论时有点不同，我可以同时做两件事。

segments.en: I can walk and chew gum.
segments.zh: 我可以走路和嚼口香糖。

segments.en: When we're talking about feelings or emotions, you say, you know, I'm happy, but at the same time I'm also scared.
segments.zh: 当我们谈论感觉或情绪时，你说，你知道，我很高兴，但同时我也很害怕。

segments.en: That means that I have these two feelings and actually they're opposite feelings.
segments.zh: 这意味着我有这两种感觉，实际上它们是相反的感觉。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Usually they are opposite feelings.
segments.zh: 通常它们是相反的感觉。

segments.en: So like you say, you're happy, but at the same time you're nervous.
segments.zh: 所以就像你说的，你很开心，但同时你也很紧张。

segments.en: It's like saying on the other hand.
segments.zh: 这就像在说 on the other hand（另一方面）。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now, when we talked about all these fears, we're afraid of flying, we are afraid of spiders.
segments.zh: 现在，当我们谈论所有这些恐惧时，我们害怕飞行，我们害怕蜘蛛。

segments.en: We describe them as a chronic fear.
segments.zh: 我们将它们描述为长期的恐惧。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this adjective chronic is very important because it has to do with time.
segments.zh: 所以 chronic 这个形容词很重要，因为它和时间有关。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I have a chronic fear of heights.
segments.zh: 所以我对高度有一种长期的恐惧。

segments.en: That means this is a fear I've always had.
segments.zh: 这意味着这是我一直以来的恐惧。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And I will always have.
segments.zh: 而且会一直有。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: You can also say she has chronic back pain.
segments.zh: 你也可以说她有慢性背痛。

segments.en: That means it comes back again and again.
segments.zh: 这意味着它一次又一次地回来。

segments.en: It's not just one time.
segments.zh: 这不仅仅是一次。

segments.en: It's all, it's some person's whole life.
segments.zh: 它是持续的，是某些人一辈子的事。

segments.en: Maybe not every day, but it comes back.
segments.zh: 也许不是每天，但它会回来。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's, if you say you have a chronic something, you're explaining that you've had it for a while or you will always have it.
segments.zh: 所以，如果你说你有个慢性的毛病，就是在说明你已经有一阵子了，或者会一直有。

segments.en: Something usually very serious also.
segments.zh: 通常也非常严重的事情。

segments.en: And going back to one of the phobias, we mentioned glossophobia and the other person said, well, you know, public speaking is not that bad.
segments.zh: 回到其中一种恐惧症，我们提到了 Glossophobia 和另一个人说，好吧，你知道，公开演讲并没有那么糟糕。

segments.en: It's not, it's not something to be so afraid of.
segments.zh: 它不是，它并没有那么值得害怕。

segments.en: And the other person replied by saying, are you kidding?
segments.zh: 另一个人回答说，你在开玩笑吗？

segments.en: Are you kidding?
segments.zh: 你开玩笑吧？

segments.en: So this is actually a way of showing some sarcasm when you're talking because public speaking is not that bad.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上是在你说话时表现出一些讽刺的一种方式，因为公开演讲并没有那么糟糕。

segments.en: The person wants to say, no, it is that bad.
segments.zh: 那个人想说，不，那就是那么糟糕。

segments.en: It is awful.
segments.zh: 太可怕了。

segments.en: So are you kidding as a way to say, no, I totally disagree.
segments.zh: 所以 are you kidding 就相当于在说，不，我完全不同意。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you're being a little bit sarcastic, but at the same time, you're also acting a bit surprised.
segments.zh: 所以你有点讽刺，但同时，你也表现得有点惊讶。

segments.en: Like, I can't believe you said that.
segments.zh: 就像，我不敢相信你这么说。

segments.en: Like if I said, I really liked the Twilight movies, Marco.
segments.zh: 就像我说的那样，我真的很喜欢暮光之城的电影，马可。

segments.en: Are you kidding?
segments.zh: 你开玩笑吧？

segments.en: Those movies are terrible.
segments.zh: 那些电影太可怕了。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So Marco does not agree with my opinion.
segments.zh: 所以马可不同意我的意见。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now, when we're talking about public speaking, we mentioned that you get on stage.
segments.zh: 现在，当我们谈论公开演讲时，我们提到你上台。

segments.en: So this is very important because this is the action to get on stage and speak.
segments.zh: 所以这非常重要，因为这是上台和说话的动作。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So if you have a stage or maybe even you don't have a stage, but you're talking about performing in front of other people, like a speech or a play, you say you get on stage and it's important to remember this as a phrase.
segments.zh: 所以如果你有一个舞台，甚至你没有一个舞台，但你是在谈论在其他人面前表演，比如演讲或戏剧，你说你上台了，把这当作一个短语很重要。

segments.en: So whenever I get on stage, I start to sweat.
segments.zh: 所以每当我上台时，我就会开始出汗。

segments.en: Now you may want to add the, there you want to say to get on the stage, but it's not necessary.
segments.zh: 现在您可能想添加，您想说上台，但这不是必需的。

segments.en: It's not incorrect, but the usual or let's say more correct form would just be, use the phrase to get on stage.
segments.zh: 这也不算错，但通常、或者说更常见的说法就是 get on stage 这个短语。

segments.en: When I get on stage, I get very nervous.
segments.zh: 当我上台时，我会非常紧张。

segments.zh: 你不必说 when I get on the stage。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: Well, I have aerophobia.
segments.zh: 嗯，我有飞行恐惧症。

segments.en: I have a chronic fear of flying.
segments.zh: 我对飞行有一种长期的恐惧。

segments.en: Oh really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: I have an uncle who is also terrified of flying.
segments.zh: 我有一个也害怕飞行的叔叔。

segments.en: It's not that bad though.
segments.zh: 不过也没那么糟糕。

segments.en: I mean, it is pretty scary to be up in this big machine flying through the air at 700 miles per hour.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，坐在这个以每小时 700 英里在空中飞行的大机器上，挺吓人的。

segments.en: I actually have arachnophobia.
segments.zh: 其实我有蜘蛛恐惧症。

segments.en: You're scared of spiders?
segments.zh: 你怕蜘蛛？

segments.en: I actually have two more phobias, acrophobia and glossophobia.
segments.zh: 其实我还有另外两种恐惧症：恐高症和公众演讲恐惧症。

segments.en: I guess that explains why you're afraid of flying, but public speaking is not that bad.
segments.zh: 我想这可以解释为什么你害怕飞行，但公开演讲并没有那么糟糕。

segments.en: Are you kidding?
segments.zh: 你开玩笑吧？

segments.en: When I get on stage, my palms start to sweat.
segments.zh: 当我上台时，我的手掌开始出汗。

segments.en: I get really nervous and I can hardly speak.
segments.zh: 我真的很紧张，我几乎不能说话。

segments.en: Well, I must confess that I am a bit claustrophobic.
segments.zh: 好吧，我必须承认我有点幽闭恐惧症。

segments.en: I hate being in an elevator for more than five seconds.
segments.zh: 我讨厌在电梯里呆了五秒钟以上。

segments.en: We are such weirdos, right?
segments.zh: 我们真是怪人，对吧？

segments.en: All right, so talking about all these phobias.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以谈谈所有这些恐惧症。

segments.en: Now one of these phobias was actually made into a movie, I think in 1990.
segments.zh: 现在，这些恐惧症里有一种还被拍成了电影，我想是在 1990 年。

segments.en: Arachnophobia, this very chronic fear of spiders.
segments.zh: 蜘蛛恐惧症，这种对蜘蛛非常长期的恐惧。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: I remember when I was younger and this movie came out, everybody started talking about how they were arachnophobic.
segments.zh: 我记得我小时候这部电影上映时，每个人都开始说自己有蜘蛛恐惧症。

segments.en: They had this horrible fear of spiders.
segments.zh: 他们对蜘蛛有这种可怕的恐惧。

segments.en: Did you ever see that movie?
segments.zh: 你看过那部电影吗？

segments.en: Yeah, of course.
segments.zh: 对，当然。

segments.en: It was terrifying.
segments.zh: 太可怕了。

segments.en: Yes, it was supposedly some South American spider that made its way into the United States in a box, in a crate or something.
segments.zh: 是的，据说是一些南美蜘蛛装在盒子或板条箱之类的东西里进入了美国。

segments.en: Now, many people handle phobias differently.
segments.zh: 现在，许多人处理恐惧症的方式不同。

segments.en: Do you have any phobia?
segments.zh: 你有恐惧症吗？

segments.en: Are you claustrophobic?
segments.zh: 你有幽闭恐惧症吗？

segments.en: Are you arachnophobic?
segments.zh: 你有蜘蛛恐惧症吗？

segments.en: I don't have any phobias and I'm not really afraid of anything.
segments.zh: 我没有任何恐惧症，我并不害怕任何事情。

segments.en: So I'm pretty lucky that way, but I know a number of people who are afraid of heights, acrophobic, and so that's pretty common.
segments.zh: 所以这方面我很幸运，但我认识一些怕高、有恐高症的人，所以这挺常见的。

segments.en: And actually, if you look it up, you will find in the dictionary maybe hundreds of phobias, people who are afraid of open spaces, people who are afraid of closed spaces, or people who are afraid of marriage.
segments.zh: 实际上，如果你查一下，你会在字典中找到数百个恐惧症，害怕开放空间的人，害怕封闭空间的人，或者害怕婚姻的人。

segments.en: They even have a phobia determined for this type of person.
segments.zh: 他们甚至对这种类型的人有一种恐惧症。

segments.en: So it's very interesting.
segments.zh: 所以这很有意思。

segments.en: Now, this is going to be a challenge.
segments.zh: 现在，这将是一个挑战。

segments.en: Why don't you look up a couple of different phobias and share it with us, maybe some of the craziest ones or the funniest ones or maybe the strangest ones you can find.
segments.zh: 你为什么不查找一些不同的恐惧症并与我们分享，也许是一些最疯狂的或最有趣的，或者你能找到的最奇怪的恐惧症。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So look them up, share them with us.
segments.zh: 所以查找它们，与我们分享。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Have a good one.
segments.zh: 祝你愉快。
